title: Calibrating Diffusion Prediction Intervals
---

**Background:** Single-stage joint diffusion models for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting couple future sky images and clear-sky index sequences, but their prediction intervals exhibit under-dispersion and systematic calibration gaps.

**Question / Future Work:** Investigate and resolve the under-dispersion and calibration gaps in predictive intervals generated by single-stage joint diffusion models, as current models tend to yield prediction intervals whose nominal coverage deviates from empirical coverage across distribution tails and varying meteorological regimes.

**Why It Matters:** Reliable probabilistic uncertainty quantification and well-calibrated prediction intervals are critical for power grid operators scheduling reserves against severe ramp events.

**Evidence:** Over nineteen nominal levels from 0.05 to 0.95, the reliability curve of the proposed model crosses the diagonal near the median rather than lying to one side of it. Empirical coverage exceeds nominal by 0.127 on average in the low tail and falls short by 0.141 in the high tail. The forecast is thus correctly centred with quantiles that are not extreme enough: the signature of under-dispersion rather than of a mis-centred forecast.
